chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you approach the Black Stone, raise your hands, praise Allah, extol Him, send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and ask Allah to accept from you. Then touch the Stone and kiss it. If you cannot kiss it, touch it with your hand. If you cannot touch it with your hand, gesture towards it and say: 'O Allah, I have fulfilled my trust and upheld my covenant, so bear witness for me with loyalty.'

O Allah, as confirmation of Your Book and upon the Sunnah of Your Prophet, I testify that there is no god except Allah Alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. I believe in Allah and disbelieve in Al-Jibt and Al-Taghut, and in Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, and in the worship of Satan and the worship of every caller invoked besides Allah.

If you cannot say all of this, say part of it, and say: 'O Allah, to You I have extended my hand, and what is with You is great in my desire, so accept my journey, forgive me, and have mercy on me. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief, poverty, and stations of shame in this world and the Hereafter.'
ai.seo_question: What is the proper supplication and etiquette when touching the Black Stone in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the ritual etiquette (adab) for the Tawaf, emphasizing the Black Stone as a covenantal witness to the pilgrim's faith. It prescribes a tiered approach for those unable to kiss the stone—touching with the hand or gesturing—while reciting a comprehensive declaration affirming monotheism and rejecting idols, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Stone as a symbolic anchor for divine testimony.
